title: Scheme selection and model portfolios
objectives: Match scheme types to client goals and risk.
body_md:
Scheme selection follows the client, not the fund.

## Steps

1. **Goal and horizon:** short (under 3 years), medium (3 to 7), long (over 7).
2. **Risk capacity and tolerance.**
3. **Choose the asset mix**, then the categories, then the schemes.
4. **Check** past consistency, costs, manager and fund house, portfolio fit, and overlap.

## Matching

| Horizon | Typical categories |
|---|---|
| Under 1 year | Overnight, liquid, ultra short, money market |
| 1 to 3 years | Short duration, corporate bond, conservative hybrid |
| 3 to 7 years | Balanced and aggressive hybrid, large-cap, flexi cap |
| Over 7 years | Equity: large, mid, flexi, index; limited small cap |

## Core and satellite

- **Core** (60 to 80%): broad, low-cost funds (index, large, flexi).
- **Satellite** (20 to 40%): focused themes, mid and small caps.

## Review

Rebalance when the mix drifts by more than a set band, or when goals change.

> **Exam tip:** Goal first, asset allocation second, scheme last.
example: A 35-year-old saving for retirement in 25 years: 70% equity (core: index and flexi cap; satellite: mid cap), 30% debt. A 55-year-old saving for a house in 2 years: mostly short duration and liquid funds.
say: We start from your goal and horizon, then pick the mix, then the funds.
Too many funds with the same stocks does not add diversification.
never: Put everything in the top-ranked fund.
Small cap funds suit a 1-year goal.
